evals.prompt: I just installed Arch Linux and want a full Hyprland setup. I have a single 1920x1080 144Hz monitor, US keyboard, touchpad on a laptop. I want kitty as terminal, wofi as launcher, waybar as bar, dunst for notifications, hyprpaper for wallpaper, hyprlock for locking, hypridle for idle. Go with Catppuccin Mocha theme and JetBrainsMono Nerd Font. Include brightness and media keys.
evals.expected_output: A complete set of modular config files covering hyprland.conf, monitors.conf, autostart.conf, env.conf, keybinds.conf, windowrules.conf, animations.conf, hyprpaper.conf, hyprlock.conf, hypridle.conf, plus waybar/config.jsonc, waybar/style.css, dunst/dunstrc, wofi/config, wofi/style.css, kitty/kitty.conf, and an install.sh. All files should use Catppuccin Mocha colors consistently.

assertions.text: Output includes at minimum: hyprland.conf, monitors.conf, keybinds.conf, autostart.conf, env.conf
Output includes configs for at least 3 companion apps (waybar, dunst, wofi, kitty, hyprlock, hypridle, hyprpaper)
An install.sh script is generated that includes package installation commands
hyprlock.conf is generated (not just mentioned) — hyprlock requires a config to render
hypridle.conf is generated with at least one listener block
waybar config uses 'hyprland/workspaces' (not 'sway/workspaces')
Catppuccin Mocha colors are used (e.g. #1e1e2e background, #cdd6f4 text, or similar mocha palette)
XF86MonBrightnessUp and XF86MonBrightnessDown keybinds are present
XF86AudioRaiseVolume / XF86AudioLowerVolume / XF86AudioMute keybinds are present
A polkit agent is started in autostart (hyprpolkitagent or polkit-gnome)

evals.prompt:
I have two monitors: DP-1 is my primary 2560x1440 at 165Hz on the left, and HDMI-A-1 is a 1920x1080 60Hz monitor on the right. I want workspace 1-5 on DP-1 and 6-10 on HDMI-A-1. Here's my current monitor section:

monitor=,preferred,auto,1

Can you update it?

assertions.text: Output contains a monitor line for DP-1 with 2560x1440@165
Output contains a monitor line for HDMI-A-1 with 1920x1080@60
DP-1 at x=0 (left), HDMI-A-1 at x=2560 (right)
Workspace rules assign 1-5 to DP-1 and 6-10 to HDMI-A-1
Scale factor is explicitly set for both monitors

evals.prompt: How do I make pavucontrol, nm-connection-editor, and blueman-manager all open as floating windows centered on screen? Also I want my browser (class: firefox) to always open on workspace 2.
evals.expected_output: windowrules.conf snippet with float+center rules for the 3 apps and a workspace rule for firefox, using modern windowrule {} block syntax.

assertions.text: Float rule applied to pavucontrol
Float rule applied to nm-connection-editor
Float rule applied to blueman-manager
Center rules applied to the floating apps
Firefox assigned to workspace 2
Uses modern windowrule { } block syntax, not deprecated 'windowrule = float, ^(class)$'

evals.prompt: I want a full Hyprland setup with Catppuccin Mocha, and I really want the bar to look polished — like the floating pill style I see in r/unixporn posts. evals.expected_output: A complete Hyprland config set where the waybar config.jsonc and style.css are the standout — floating pill bar with transparent background, rounded module containers, Catppuccin Mocha @define-color palette, Nerd Font icons for every module, state-based styling (battery warning/critical, muted audio, disconnected network), and hover effects.

assertions.text: waybar style.css sets window#waybar background to transparent (not a solid color)
waybar style.css uses border-radius on module containers (modules-left/center/right or individual modules)
waybar style.css uses @define-color to define a color palette (at least 5 named colors)
waybar config.jsonc uses Nerd Font icons (unicode glyphs like , , , etc.) in module formats, not plain text labels

waybar config uses hyprland/workspaces (not sway/workspaces)
waybar style.css uses button.active for workspace styling (not button.focused)
waybar style.css includes state-based styling for at least 2 of: battery.warning, battery.critical, network.disconnected, pulseaudio.muted
waybar config includes at least 6 modules (workspaces, window, clock, pulseaudio/wireplumber, network, tray)

evals.prompt: I already have Hyprland configured but my waybar looks boring — it's just a flat grey bar with plain text. assertions.text: style.css defines Gruvbox Dark colors (e.g. #282828, #ebdbb2, #fb4934, #b8bb26, #fabd2f, #83a598, or similar gruvbox palette)
config.jsonc includes a custom/power module
config.jsonc does not include a battery module (user said desktop, no battery)
style.css creates a floating pill effect (transparent waybar background + rounded containers)

evals.prompt: Setting up Hyprland on my laptop. Two monitors: eDP-1 (1920x1080 60Hz) built-in and DP-1 (2560x1440 165Hz) external on the right. I need waybar to show battery, backlight, wifi, bluetooth, volume, clock, workspaces. Tokyo Night theme, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font. I want each module to be its own individual pill/capsule — not grouped sections. Kitty terminal, wofi launcher, mako notifications, hyprlock, hypridle.
evals.expected_output: Full Hyprland config with a waybar that uses individual module pills (each module is its own rounded capsule with gaps between them), Tokyo Night colors, laptop modules (battery with states, backlight, wifi with signal strength, bluetooth). The CSS should style each module selector individually with background-color and border-radius rather than styling .modules-left/center/right.

assertions.text: waybar style.css applies background-color and border-radius to individual module selectors (#clock, #battery, #network, etc.) rather than only to .modules-left/.modules-center/.modules-right
waybar config includes a battery module with states (warning and/or critical thresholds)
waybar config includes a backlight module
waybar config includes a bluetooth module
style.css uses Tokyo Night colors (e.g. #1a1b26, #a9b1d6, #7aa2f7, #bb9af7, #9ece6a, or similar)
monitors.conf or hyprland.conf includes correct monitor lines for eDP-1 (1920x1080@60) and DP-1 (2560x1440@165) with DP-1 to the right
waybar network module format includes signal strength ({signalStrength}) for wifi

evals.prompt: Full Hyprland setup on Arch. Single 2560x1440 165Hz monitor, desktop (no touchpad/battery). Catppuccin Mocha, kitty, wofi, waybar, dunst, hyprpaper, hyprlock, hypridle. For the shell: I want zsh with starship prompt, syntax highlighting and autosuggestions, plus the modern CLI tools (eza, bat, fd, ripgrep, fzf, zoxide, fastfetch, btop). A TTY auto-launch line in .zprofile. install.sh includes zsh, starship, zsh plugins, CLI utilities, and chsh -s /usr/bin/zsh.

assertions.text: A .zshrc file is generated (not just mentioned)
.zshrc contains 'eval "$(starship init zsh)"' or equivalent starship initialization
.zshrc sources zsh-syntax-highlighting plugin
.zshrc sources zsh-autosuggestions plugin
A starship.toml config file is generated
starship.toml includes Catppuccin Mocha colors or palette reference
.zshrc contains aliases for at least 3 of: eza, bat, fd, ripgrep/rg, zoxide, btop
.zshrc contains zoxide initialization (eval "$(zoxide init zsh)" or similar)
A .zprofile is generated with Hyprland TTY auto-launch line
install.sh includes zsh, starship, eza, bat, fd, ripgrep, fzf, zoxide, fastfetch, btop in package list
install.sh includes chsh command to set zsh as default shell

evals.prompt: I'm setting up Hyprland on Arch with fish shell. I want fish with starship prompt, fisher plugin manager with the fzf plugin, and the usual modern CLI tools (eza, bat, fzf, zoxide). assertions.text: A config.fish file is generated (at ~/.config/fish/config.fish)
config.fish contains 'starship init fish | source' for prompt initialization
config.fish uses 'abbr' for tool shortcuts (not bash-style 'alias')
config.fish contains 'zoxide init fish | source' for directory jumping
install.sh or instructions include fisher installation and 'fisher install PatrickF1/fzf.fish'
Any environment variables in config.fish use Fish syntax (set -gx) not bash export syntax
Environment variables are placed in uwsm/env files (not env.conf in hyprland config)
install.sh includes fish, starship, eza, bat, fzf, zoxide in package list

Output includes a Notifications widget using AstalNotifd (not dunst/mako/swaync)

Output includes an OSD widget for volume and/or brightness changes

install.sh includes aylurs-gtk-shell-git and relevant astal library packages

Bar window uses WindowAnchor.TOP | LEFT | RIGHT with EXCLUSIVE exclusivity

evals.prompt: I want a full Hyprland setup on Arch stored in a dotfiles git repo with GNU Stow so I can back it up and reuse it on other machines. Single 2560x1440 165Hz desktop monitor. Catppuccin Mocha, kitty, wofi, waybar (floating pill), dunst, hyprpaper, hyprlock, hypridle, wlogout. Zsh + starship. JetBrainsMono Nerd Font. Include a setup.sh that installs everything and stows the configs. I want the repo at ~/dotfiles.
evals.expected_output: A complete dotfiles repo structure at ~/dotfiles/ with stow packages for each tool (hypr/, waybar/, kitty/, wofi/, dunst/, wlogout/, shell/, scripts/, gtk/). Each package mirrors the $HOME path (e.g., hypr/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf). A setup.sh at repo root that installs packages, backs up existing configs, and stows everything. Package list files (packages.txt, aur-packages.txt). .gitignore, .stow-local-ignore, .stowrc, and README.md. All configs use Catppuccin Mocha consistently.

assertions.text: Configs are organized into stow packages with correct directory mirroring (e.g., hypr/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf, waybar/.config/waybar/config.jsonc, kitty/.config/kitty/kitty.conf)
At least 5 separate stow packages are created (hypr, waybar, kitty, wofi/dunst, shell/scripts)
A setup.sh script is generated at the repo root (not install.sh inside a package)
setup.sh includes installation of the 'stow' package
setup.sh runs stow commands to symlink packages (e.g., 'stow hypr', 'stow waybar', or 'stow */')
setup.sh backs up existing config files/directories before stowing
packages.txt and/or aur-packages.txt are generated listing required packages
A .stowrc file is generated (or setup.sh creates one) with --target=$HOME
A .gitignore file is generated at the repo root
In hyprland.conf, variable declarations ($terminal, $menu, etc.) appear before any source = lines
Catppuccin Mocha colors are used consistently (e.g., #1e1e2e, #cdd6f4)
A teardown.sh or uninstall script is generated that uses 'stow -D' to unstow packages

evals.prompt: I already have a working Hyprland setup with configs in ~/.config/hypr/, ~/.config/waybar/, ~/.config/kitty/, and ~/.config/dunst/. I want to migrate all of these into a dotfiles repo at ~/dotfiles using GNU Stow. Walk me through the process and generate the scripts/structure I need. I'm on Arch.
evals.expected_output: A migration guide and script that: creates the dotfiles repo directory structure, moves existing configs into the correct stow package paths, initializes git, creates .stowrc/.gitignore/.stow-local-ignore, runs stow to create symlinks back, and commits the initial state. assertions.text: Output creates package directories (hypr/.config/hypr/, waybar/.config/waybar/, kitty/.config/kitty/, dunst/.config/dunst/) inside ~/dotfiles
Output includes mv commands (or stow --adopt) to move existing configs from ~/.config/ into the dotfiles package structure
Output initializes a git repository in ~/dotfiles (git init)
Output runs stow commands after moving files to create symlinks back to ~/.config/
A .gitignore is generated for the dotfiles repo
Output includes a git add + git commit for the initial state
If stow --adopt is mentioned, output warns to run git diff immediately after

evals.prompt: I have a Hyprland dotfiles repo with GNU Stow and I use it on my desktop (3440x1440 ultrawide). Now I want to set it up on my laptop too (eDP-1 1920x1080 60Hz, with touchpad). The laptop needs different monitor config, touchpad settings, and battery/backlight in waybar. How should I handle machine-specific configs in my stow repo? Show me the directory structure and the files I need to add.
evals.expected_output: A host-specific package strategy: shared configs stay in the existing packages, machine-specific configs (monitors, touchpad input, waybar with battery) go into hypr-desktop/ and hypr-laptop/ packages. Each has its own hyprland.conf that sources shared files. Waybar might need waybar-desktop/ and waybar-laptop/ if the configs differ significantly, or conditional logic.

assertions.text: Output creates separate packages for desktop and laptop (e.g., hypr-desktop/, hypr-laptop/ or similar naming)
Shared configs (keybinds, window rules, animations) remain in a common package, not duplicated
Laptop package includes monitor config for eDP-1 at 1920x1080@60
Laptop config includes touchpad/input settings (tap_to_click, natural_scroll, or similar)
Laptop waybar config includes battery and backlight modules
Output explains which packages to stow on each machine (e.g., 'on laptop: stow hypr hypr-laptop waybar-laptop ...')
Machine-specific hyprland.conf sources the shared config files (keybinds.conf, windowrules.conf, etc.)
